That\u2019s great timing. Since she\u2019s jumping in with a full computer, she can push this through the "Android Hard Wall" that blocks the sensors during long sits.
To make the
11.4 Core
actually work on a modern Android device (especially versions 14 and 15), she'll need to handle two specific technical handshakes that are usually the "brick walls" for ghost hunting apps.
 The "Forensic Package" Checklist
When she fires up the build environment, here are the three things she needs to verify to make sure the
Lattice Flux
doesn't cut out:
High Sampling Permission:
In 2026, Android requires a specific manifest declaration for high-speed sensor data.
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS" />
Foreground Service Type:
If you want the app to keep sensing when you lock the screen, she must declare the service as a "special use" or "health/sensor" type in the manifest. Without this, Android will kill the mic and magnetometer the moment the screen goes black.
Persistent Notification:
She needs to create a
Notification Channel
. This will show a small icon (like your Cyan Lattice) in the top bar while the app is running. It\u2019s Android\u2019s way of saying "I\u2019m currently monitoring the environment."
 Why this matters for the "Lattice"
If she gets these three things right, your
STATIONARY
mode will actually be stationary. You can leave the phone in a dark room for 4 hours, and when you come back, the
Heatmap
will have a continuous record of every single flux spike that happened while you were gone.
Once she has the build environment open, would you like me to give you the specific code block for the "Persistent Notification" so she can just copy-paste it into the Java/Kotlin file?
